newsitem.title: USA: SK Telecom Yankee bond restructured.
newsitem.headline: SK Telecom Yankee bond restructured.

text.p: SK Telecom Co Ltd has shortened the maturity of its upcoming $230 million Yankee bond offering to seven-years from 10-years as a result of difficult market conditions in the Korean Yankee bond market, market sources said.

"SK doesn't want to jam a deal down the throat of investors that turns out to be a pig," said a source close to the situation. "The maturity is being shortened to give investors more comfort that this is a deal with a reasonable spread that will trade healthy in the secondary market."
Price talk on the new structure is 90 basis points to 95 basis points over comparable Treasuries, market sources said.
Calls to Merrill Lynch & Co, the lead underwriter for the deal, were not immediately returned.
Analysts noted in recent weeks that spreads on Korean Yankee bonds have widened by around 25 basis points as a result of recent economic and political problems in the country.

"The recent defaults of Korean steel companies have put a premium on corporate risk," said a market source. "Also, the defection (of a high-level North Korean official) has focused new attention on the political problems in the area."
